contentHtml:
In this blog, we'll talk about how to take Vitamin D supplements, it's surprising benefits, and easy ways to get more vitamin D naturally.

Vitamin D, also known as the “sunshine vitamin,” is super important for more than just your bones! It helps keep your body strong and healthy by supporting your immune system, mental health, and doing a lot more.

What is Vitamin D?

Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin, which means your body needs fat to absorb it properly. It helps your body absorb calcium and phosphorus. These needed to keep your bones and teeth strong.

Vitamin D also helps with things like your immune system, cell growth, and reducing inflammation. There are two main types of vitamin D: vitamin D2 and vitamin D3. Vitamin D3 is better because it’s more effective at raising your vitamin D levels in the blood.

How to Get Vitamin D

The best way to get vitamin D is naturally from the sunlight. When sunlight hits your skin, your body starts making vitamin D. However, things like your skin type, the time of day, and where you live can affect how much vitamin D you make from the sun.

How to Get Vitamin D from the Sun

In India, the best time to get vitamin D from the sun is between 6 and 8 am. During this time, the sun’s rays are strong enough for your body to make vitamin D. But be careful! Too much sun without protection can harm your skin. Aim for about 10–30 minutes of sun exposure each day to get enough vitamin D.

How to Increase Vitamin D

If you’re not getting enough vitamin D from sunlight or food, you might wonder how to increase vitamin D. One easy way is by taking vitamin D supplements. These are especially helpful if you don’t get enough vitamin D from the sun.

You can also get more vitamin D from certain foods. Here are some vitamin D-rich foods you can try:

  • Fatty fish (like salmon, mackerel, or sardines)
  • Fortified dairy products (like milk or yoghurt)
  • Fortified cereals
  • Egg yolks
  • Beef liver

If you’re vegetarian or vegan, you can go for fortified plant-based milks or UV-exposed mushrooms. These are great plant-based sources of vitamin D!

Vitamin D3 Supplement: Benefits and How to Take It

Taking vitamin D3 supplements can really help if you're not getting enough from food or sunlight. Here are 5 awesome benefits of vitamin D, especially for your gut health!

1. Supports Strong Bones

Vitamin D3 helps your body absorb calcium, which is super important for strong bones and teeth. Without enough vitamin D, your bones can become weak and break easily. If you're an adult, taking vitamin D supplements can help maintain healthy bones and reduce the risk of fractures.

2. Boosts Your Immune System

Vitamin D is key to keeping your immune system strong. It helps your body fight off germs, like bacteria and viruses. If you don’t get enough vitamin D, you might get sick more often. Taking a vitamin D supplement can help protect you from infections, especially during cold and flu season.

3. Improves Mood and Mental Health

Did you know that vitamin D can affect your mood? People with low vitamin D levels are more likely to feel depressed or anxious. Taking vitamin D tablets can help boost your mood and reduce feelings of anxiety or sadness.

4. Helps Gut Health & Hormone Balance

Vitamin D is important for keeping your gut healthy. Here are 5 ways vitamin D helps your gut:

  • Leaky Gut:

    Vitamin D helps keep your gut lining strong. This is important because if the lining becomes weak, it can lead to a leaky gut. Then, food particles, toxins and harmful substances leak into your bloodstream. This can cause inflammation. Vitamin D helps prevent this. Check out 10 signs of an unhealthy gut.

  • IBS:

    If you have Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS), vitamin D can help reduce inflammation in your gut and make digestion easier.

  • IBD:

    If you have Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), which includes conditions like Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, vitamin D can help control the inflammation in your gut.

  • Gut-Brain Connection:

    Your gut health affects your brain. Vitamin D can help balance serotonin (a mood-regulating chemical) and improve both your gut and mental health.

  • Hormonal Issues (like PCOS):

    Vitamin D is important for hormone balance. If you have PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome), vitamin D can help regulate your hormones and improve your overall health. Take a look at our Indian diet plan for PCOS.

    Vitamin D is also helpful in managing diabetes. That is why sometimes it is considered a hormone, and not just a vitamin.

5. Supports Heart Health

Vitamin D helps keep your heart healthy. Studies show that not getting enough vitamin D can increase the risk of heart problems like high blood pressure, heart attacks, and strokes. So, taking vitamin D supplements can help protect your heart.

6. Should You Take Vitamin K2 and Magnesium with Vitamin D Supplements?

Yes, it's often a good idea to take vitamin K2 and magnesium with vitamin D supplements. Here’s why this combination supports better health and makes your supplement routine more effective:

Why Take Vitamin K2 with Vitamin D?

  • Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium, but it doesn't control where the calcium goes.
  • Vitamin K2 directs calcium to your bones and teeth, and keeps it out of your arteries and soft tissues — helping prevent hardening of the arteries.
  • Taking K2 with D3 can improve bone and heart health.

Why Add Magnesium?

  • Magnesium helps activate vitamin D in the body so it can do its job.
  • Without enough magnesium, vitamin D may not work properly, and you could end up with symptoms of vitamin D deficiency even if you're supplementing.
  • It also supports muscle function, nerve health, and mood balance.

Here is a list of 10 magnesium-rich foods.

How to Take Them Together:

  • Choose a vitamin D3 supplement that includes K2 (MK-7).
  • Add magnesium glycinate or citrate, especially if your diet is low in magnesium-rich foods.
  • Take them with a meal that contains fat for better absorption.

What Happens If Vitamin D is Low?

If you don’t have enough vitamin D, it can lead to some issues. Here are some vitamin D deficiency symptoms:

  • Tiredness or fatigue
  • Bone pain or muscle weakness
  • Hair loss
  • Weak immune system (getting sick more often)

Does Vitamin D Deficiency Cause Hair Loss?

Yes, vitamin D deficiency can cause hair loss. It can lead to conditions like alopecia areata, where hair falls out in patches. If you think you might be low in vitamin D, getting more through the sun, food, or supplements can help.

Vitamin D Deficiency Diseases

If you don’t get enough vitamin D, it can lead to problems like:

  • Rickets: Affects bone growth in children.
  • Osteomalacia: Causes weak bones and muscles in adults.
  • Osteoporosis: Makes bones brittle and fragile, increasing the risk of fractures. Osteoporosis is common among post-menopausal women. This is due to the decrease in estrogen levels. Take a look at 7 calcium-rich foods for women in the menopausal stage.

Vitamin D Supplements: Tablets or Capsules?

When deciding whether to take vitamin D3 tablets or capsules, it mostly comes down to what’s easier for you to swallow. Both types work the same way, so pick whichever is more comfortable!

Best Vitamin D Supplement

When looking for the best vitamin D3 supplement, choose one that has vitamin D3 (it’s the most effective type). Vitamin D3 usually comes from animal sources like fish oil. But if you’re vegan, look for plant-based supplements made from lichen.

How Much Vitamin D Per Day?

The recommended amount of vitamin D depends on your age and health. For most people, it’s about 600–800 IU per day. However, if you’re low in vitamin D, your doctor might recommend a higher dose.

Conclusion: How to Take Vitamin D Supplement for Better Health

Taking a vitamin D supplement is an easy way to keep your body healthy, especially if you're not getting enough from the sun or food. Whether you're looking to improve your bones, immune system, or help your gut, vitamin D has lots of benefits.

Don't forget, you can also increase your vitamin D levels by getting some sun, eating vitamin D-rich foods, and considering the best vitamin D supplement for you.
